item.title: Direct mass measurements of the high-spin isomers in self-conjugate 94Ag
item.description: arXiv:2611.34355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two decades ago, two-proton emission from a $(21^+)$ isomeric state in $^{94}$Ag was reported. This report has remained the sole example of possible two-proton radioactivity in a nucleus with an odd number of protons on the chart of nuclei. A debate regarding the viability of the decay mode has been ongoing due to the unknown mass of the isomer. Here, using state-selective laser ionization in a hot cavity catcher, we present multi-reflection time-of-flight mass spectrometry of the long-lived isomeric states of $^{94}$Ag and its one-proton decay daughter $^{93}$Pd. For the first time, direct mass measurements of the $(7^+)$ and $(21^+)$ isomeric states set the stage for an independent discussion of the energetics of these decays. We rule out the two-proton emission from the $(21^+)$ state as previously reported and reveal the one-proton decay energy to be significantly lower. State-of-the-art shell-model calculations reproduce the energy gap of the $(7^+)$ and the $(21^+)$ states as well as the half-life of the $(21^+)$ state, implying the $(21^+)$ state is likely near-spherical, contradicting the reported explanation for the two-proton radioactivity. Importantly, the techniques employed are a stepping stone towards the first laser spectroscopic investigation of a proton-emitting state

item.title: Nuclear Modification of $\pi^0$ Production in pO and OO Collisions with ALICE
item.description: arXiv:2611.34503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Energy loss of high-momentum partons is one of the key signatures of the quark--gluon plasma formed in heavy-ion collisions. Through measurements of the nuclear modification factor, $R_{\rm AA}$, where a strong suppression of high-$p_{\rm T}$ particle yields is observed, parton energy loss has been confirmed in Pb--Pb collisions at the LHC. However, in small collision systems, like pp and p--Pb, energy loss has not yet been confirmed. In this contribution, a measurement of the $\pi^0$ $R_{\rm AA}$ in OO and pO collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.36$ TeV and $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 9.62$ TeV, respectively, is presented. These results are based on the measured $\pi^0$ $p_{\rm T}$ spectra in OO, pO, and pp collisions using the ALICE electromagnetic calorimeter. The measurement of the $R_{\rm pO}$ allows for precise constraints on cold-nuclear matter effects. In combination with the $R_{\rm OO}$, this allows for a separation of cold and hot nuclear matter contributions and enables a quantitative determination of partonic energy loss in OO collisions. The measurements are compared to theoretical model calculations that include both cold and hot nuclear matter effects.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Strangmann

item.title: QED corrections to neutron and nuclear $\beta$-decay at order $\alpha^2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.34804v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute two-loop QED corrections to neutron and nuclear beta decay, including full electron mass dependence and real radiation contributions. The result for the neutron, $\delta_{R,\,\rm static}= ( 29.199 \pm 0.001 )\times 10^{-3}$, implies a factor $\sim 70 $ reduction in the uncertainty of the low-energy radiative corrections compared to previous results obtained in the large energy/small electron-mass limit, $m_e/(m_n-m_p) \to 0$. For superallowed nuclear decays we find that the $Z$-independent order $\alpha^2$ corrections range from $(0.1-0.5) \times 10^{-4}$ i.e., of roughly the expected size and comparable to current uncertainty estimates.
item.dc:creator: Zehua Cao, Richard J. Hill, Ryan Plestid, Peter Vander Griend

item.title: Electromagnetic Radiation from Baryon-Rich Matter in Heavy-Ion Collisions
item.description: arXiv:2511.08773v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We perform a study of electromagnetic radiation in heavy-ion collisions at Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) Beam Energy Scan (BES) and SPS energies using the iEBE-MUSIC framework, which includes 3D dynamical Monte Carlo Glauber initial conditions, MUSIC (3+1)D viscous relativistic hydrodynamics, and the UrQMD hadronic afterburner. The multistage modeling has been calibrated to hadronic data at RHIC-BES energies using a Bayesian analysis. Integrating the thermal photon emission rates with the medium evolution, we study the direct photon yield and elliptic flow and how they vary with collision energy and emission source. We compare with results obtained by the STAR and PHENIX Collaborations. We employ next-to-leading order thermal QCD dilepton emission rates to compute dilepton invariant mass spectra and extract the effective temperature of the quark-gluon plasma at different collision energies.
item.dc:creator: Xiang-Yu Wu, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon, Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Paquet, Bj\"orn Schenke, Chun Shen

item.title: Probing gluon saturation with forward di-hadron correlations in proton-nucleus collisions
item.description: arXiv:2512.21466v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a detailed numerical investigation of semi-inclusive forward di-hadron production in proton--nucleus collisions employing the Color Glass Condensate effective theory. We focus on the regime where di-hadrons are produced nearly back-to-back in the transverse plane, thereby justifying a transverse-momentum-dependent factorization approach in terms of small-$x$ gluon distributions. Our computation integrates several key elements: i) non-linear rapidity evolution via the Balitsky--Kovchegov equation with running coupling, ii) both perturbative and non-perturbative Sudakov resummation, and iii) a phenomenologically constrained model for the initial conditions for small-$x$ gluon distributions. We compare this phenomenological framework to experimental data from the STAR Collaboration on azimuthal correlations in forward di-pion production in both proton--proton and proton--gold collisions. We analyze the systematic theoretical uncertainties associated with the saturation scales of nuclei at the initial scale for rapidity evolution and with those associated with the hadronization process. Finally, we make predictions for the kinematics anticipated to be covered by the ALICE Forward Calorimeter (FoCal) upgrade at the Large Hadron Collider.
item.dc:creator: Paul Caucal, Zhong-Bo Kang, Piotr Korcyl, Farid Salazar, Bj\"orn Schenke, Tomasz Stebel, Raju Venugopalan, Wenbin Zhao

item.title: Data Unfolding: From Problem Formulation to Result Assessment
item.description: arXiv:2603.03168v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Experimental data in particle and nuclear physics, particle astrophysics, and radiation protection dosimetry are collected using experimental facilities that consist of a complex system of sensors, electronics, and software. Measured spectra or cross sections are considered as Probability Density Functions (PDFs) that deviate from true PDFs due to resolution, bias, and efficiency effects. Unfolding is viewed as a procedure for estimating an unknown true PDF. Reliable estimates of the true PDF are necessary for testing theoretical models, comparing results from different experiments, and combining results from various research endeavors. Both external and internal quality assessment methods can be applied for this purpose. In some cases, external criteria exist to evaluate deconvolution quality. A typical example is the deconvolution of a blurred image, where the sharpness of the restored image serves as an indicator of quality. However, defining such external criteria can be challenging, particularly when a measurement has not been performed previously. This paper discusses various internal criteria for assessing the quality of the results independently of external information, as well as factors that influence the quality of the unfolded distribution.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay D. Gagunashvili

item.title: Sensitivity of Electromagnetic Moments to Nuclear Forces
item.description: arXiv:2603.26905v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Nuclear electromagnetic moments can be precisely measured across the nuclear chart, yet understanding how they emerge from the underlying nuclear force is an open challenge for nuclear theory. Using a global emulator of ab initio calculations, we show that, unlike binding energies and charge radii, magnetic and quadrupole moments probe components of the chiral interaction that vary strongly with neutron number. We demonstrate this sensitivity with the properties of calcium isotopes, where measured moments reveal information that is largely hidden from bulk observables. We then demonstrate a method to address the inverse problem, using selected experimental magnetic moments to constrain and reorganize the allowed parameter space of the nuclear force, improving predictions beyond the calibration set while preserving descriptions of other nuclear properties.
item.dc:creator: Jose M. Munoz, Antoine Belley, Andreas Ekstr\"om, Gaute Hagen, Jason D. Holt, Ronald F. Garcia Ruiz

item.title: Light-by-light scattering: asymptotic expansions, Coulomb resummation and NLO corrections
item.description: arXiv:2604.00099v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Light-by-light (LbL) scattering is one of the earliest predictions of quantum electrodynamics (QED). Interest in this process has been renewed following its experimental observation at the LHC and the prospects of future measurements at free-electron laser facilities. In this paper, we refine theoretical predictions for LbL scattering by improving the full fermion-mass-dependent two-loop QCD and QED helicity amplitudes using high- and low-energy asymptotic expansions, and by performing Coulomb resummation in the threshold region. The $W$-boson contribution, relevant when the di-photon invariant mass exceeds twice the $W$-boson mass, is included at one-loop accuracy. We present state-of-the-art predictions for LbL cross sections in the Standard Model and provide a new event generator, LbLatNLO, for Monte Carlo simulations of LbL scattering.
item.dc:creator: Ajjath A H, Ekta Chaubey, Hua-Sheng Shao

item.title: The production of lepton pairs in heavy-ion collisions at SPS and RHIC energies
item.description: arXiv:2611.23506v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We perform a quantitative study of dilepton production and elliptic flow in In+In collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=17.3$ GeV and isobar collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}=200$ GeV, concentrating on the low and intermediate invariant mass regions. The medium evolution is simulated event-by-event with the multistage iEBE-MUSIC framework, and the electromagnetic emission combines for the first time quark-gluon plasma (QGP) emission calculated at next-to-leading order (NLO) in the strong coupling with in-medium radiation calculated with hadronic many-body theory. Freeze-out and surviving primordial $\rho$ decays are also included. The calculations are compared with the high-precision dimuon spectra measured by the NA60 Collaboration, and with STAR preliminary measurements of dielectron spectra and elliptic flow. We obtain effective temperatures extracted from the transverse-mass spectra, and we calculate the elliptic flow of the different dilepton sources. Our results suggest that dilepton measurements in the low-mass and high $p_T$ region can provide insight into higher-order corrections to the QGP emission rate.
item.dc:creator: Xiang-Yu Wu, Han Gao, Charles Gale, Sangyong Jeon, Ralf Rapp
